<subject>Re: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Halcyon's Issues With Credit Risk</subject>
<body>
You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the lenders on HALO.  Reply to the email below once you find out if you are able to use the lender's funds without maintaining a balance.
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From:  Owen, Julia  
Sent:  Tuesday, 29 April 2025 16:09
To:  Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc:  Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject:  Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Halcyon's  Issues With Credit Risk

Here is a quick update on how Aurora Finance, Halcyon, bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Credit Risk issues:

Aurora Finance agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Credit Risk.  The lender admitted that Credit Risk has been using their loan contracts and have been paying their bills since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £1.5 million claim that Aurora Finance had been including in the Halcyon "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining demand charges for Credit Risk's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out of Aurora Finance's Motion.
The minimum loan/pooling agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the lender (Note:  Originally Aurora Finance appeared to be using Credit Risk's minimum balance to set off Treasury & Credit Risk obligations). 

I would recommend that you challenge Aurora Finance's operations folks, if they continue to say that Credit Risk must be keeping a minimum balance in your loan account.  If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen
</quoted>
